data.long_meaning: Baikunth is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Vaikuntha' or 'Baikuntha'. It refers to the celestial abode of Lord Vishnu, where the souls of the virtuous go after death. This name is believed to bring blessings of prosperity, peace, and spiritual growth.

in_sanskrit.name: वैकुंथ
in_sanskrit.meaning: Sky or heaven filled with bliss
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: वै (vai) - all, कुंथ (kunth) - sky, filled, heaven. So, Baikunth means a sky or heaven filled with bliss.

in_hindi.name: वैकुंथ
in_hindi.meaning: समस्या से मुक्त राहें वापस लाने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: वै (vai) - समस्या (problem), कुंथ (kunth) - उत्पत्ति (origination), वाला (vala) - one who brings back. So, Baikunth means one who brings back solutions to problems.

in_tamil.name: வைகுந்த
in_tamil.meaning: வாய் (vai) - all, குஞ்சி (kunth) - sky, filled, heaven. So, Baikunth means a sky or heaven filled with bliss.

in_telugu.name: వైకుంఠ
in_telugu.long_meaning: వై (vai) - శ్శోదర్ (supreme), కుంఠ (kunth) - మూదేశపూజీ (deity of the mind), So, Baikunth means the supreme deity of the mind.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Baikunth" carries deep cultural significance in Hinduism as it alludes to the divine and ethereal world of the Lord Vishnu. Naming a child as Baikunth is considered auspicious as it is believed to confer protection, prosperity, and spiritual growth. It is also associated with the traditions and rituals revolving around Lord Vishnu, invoking the virtues of truth, compassion, and forgiveness.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Baikunth" is rooted in Hinduism's concept of Moksha - the ultimate goal of liberation from the cycle of birth and death. The name signifies the journey towards the divine realm of Lord Vishnu, a place of peace, harmony, and enlightenment. Thus, it serves as a constant reminder of the eternity, divinity, and spiritual pursuits of life. In essence, the name Baikunth bestows the power and strength of Lord Vishnu to help the person navigate through life's challenges, seeking the path towards peace and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Baikunth Meghwal was a great poet and scholar from Rajasthan, India, who lived in the 16th century. He is known for his works in Marathi and Sanskrit languages, particularly for his epic poem 'Krishna Karuna.'

Another mention of Baikunth comes from the Bhagavata Purana, a major Hindu scripture narrating the story of God Krishna. In one chapter, Krishna himself reveals to Uddhava that those who remember Him as Baikuntha attain salvation in Vaikuntha, the celestial abode of Vishnu.
